procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Feels about the same as fall. Stairs with one rest. Daily weights 86 to 88 kg. No orthopnea. Hands and legs unchanged; neurology every 6 months.
Exam: no JVD, lungs clear, trace edema at the ankles, heart regular.
Plan: continue furosemide, empagliflozin, amlodipine, metformin, glyburide, atorvastatin, aspirin, tamsulosin, finasteride. Labs today. 3 months.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Doing well. Spring pollen, used albuterol a few times in April, fine now. Weight stable. No falls.
Lungs clear today, no edema beyond trace.
No changes. Refills for 90 days sent. RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Pharmacy question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Marc here. The pharmacy says Dad's finasteride needs a new prescription, the urologist retired. Can you send it?

documents.title: RE: Pharmacy question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sent finasteride 5 mg, 90 days with 3 refills. He can stay on it with tamsulosin; let me know if his urine stream gets worse and we can find him a new urologist.

documents.title: Optometry diabetic eye exam
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated diabetic eye exam 08/17/2023. No diabetic retinopathy. Pseudophakia OD. Mild nuclear sclerosis OS, stable. Recall 1 year.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Per PCP standing order, given flu high-dose (L deltoid), RSV (R deltoid) and the updated COVID (R deltoid, 1 inch below). He and son agreed to all three at once to save a trip. Observed 15 min, fine. Told sore arms and a tired day are common.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV with wife.
Function: self-care independent, IADLs mostly by wife. No falls. Cane outdoors.
PHQ-2 0.
Vaccines current for the season.
Advance care planning (separate time, about 20 min): reviewed his values with him and his wife. He would want CPR and hospital care if there is a good chance of getting back home; would not want to be kept on machines long term if he could not recognize family. Wife remains proxy, son alternate. MOLST not completed today, he wants to think it over.
Labs today. RTC 3 months.

reports.text: Sinus tachycardia, rate 110. ST segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF. Compared with outpatient tracing 07/2022, the inferior ST elevation is new.
reports.conclusion: Acute inferior ST elevation myocardial infarction.

reports.text: Access: right radial artery. Left main normal. Left anterior descending and left circumflex without flow-limiting disease. Right coronary artery: acute occlusion, culprit for the inferior STEMI. Primary PCI with one drug-eluting stent deployed with TIMI 3 flow restored. Radial band applied, no complications.
reports.conclusion: Culprit RCA occlusion treated with a single drug-eluting stent.

reports.text: Left ventricle mildly dilated. Inferior wall hypokinesis. LVEF 50%. No significant valvular disease. No pericardial effusion. Right ventricle normal.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Arrival 08/01/2024 07:45 by ambulance, wife following.

CC: chest pain.
HPI: 73 yo man with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, hyperlipidemia and prior heart failure. Two hours of abrupt, severe pressure in the chest spreading to the left arm, 9/10, with nausea and sweating. Began at rest after waking.
Meds per wife: metformin, lisinopril, atorvastatin, glyburide 5 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily, albuterol inhaler as needed.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
Exam: diaphoretic, uncomfortable. BP 160/90, HR 110, RR 22. Heart tachycardic, regular, no murmur. Lungs clear.
ECG: ST elevation II, III, aVF.
Troponin I 8.0 ng/mL (ref <0.04). CK-MB 50 U/L (ref 0-24). Myoglobin 150 mcg/L (ref 28-72).

Assessment: acute inferior STEMI. Cath lab activated at 07:58, aspirin load and heparin given, ticagrelor deferred to cardiology. To cath lab 08:30.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, cardiology service. Admitted 08/01/2024, discharged 08/04/2024.

Principal diagnosis: acute ST elevation MI, inferior wall, right coronary artery.
Procedure 08/01: emergent coronary angiography via right radial artery. Acute RCA occlusion; primary PCI with one drug-eluting stent, TIMI 3 flow. Other vessels without flow-limiting disease.
Course: chest pain resolved after PCI. Monitored in the CCU overnight, no arrhythmia. Echo 08/02: LVEF 50%, inferior hypokinesis. Ambulating independently with cane by day 2.

Discharge medications:
- Aspirin 81 mg daily
- Clopidogrel 75 mg daily for at least 12 months (chosen over ticagrelor given age and fall risk)
- Atorvastatin 80 mg daily (increased from 40)
- Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily (new)
- Continue furosemide 40 mg, empagliflozin 10 mg, amlodipine 5 mg, metformin, glyburide, tamsulosin, finasteride, albuterol as needed
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week, cardiology 6 weeks, cardiac rehab referral sent. Do not stop clopidogrel without speaking to cardiology.

conditions.label: ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction involving right coronary artery

documents.title: Wife calling, husband in hospital
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Wife called from the hospital. Leonard had a heart attack yesterday morning, ambulance to the regional hospital, they put a stent in the right side artery the same morning. In the CCU, sitting up, eating. Expected home over the weekend.
Told her to call when discharged and we will see him within the week. Hospital records requested.

documents.title: RE: Wife calling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Front desk please hold a transitional visit slot for next Thursday.

medications.drug: 24 HR metoprolol succinate 25 MG Extended Release Oral Tablet

documents.title: Transitional Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Discharged 8/4 after inferior STEMI with a stent to the RCA (per wife and the discharge paperwork she brought, a single page med list; full hospital records not yet received). Wife called us 8/2 while he was still inpatient.

S: no chest pain since the procedure. Tired. Walking the house and the driveway. Right wrist sore where they went in. No bleeding, no black stools. No palpitations or lightheadedness. Weights steady.

Med reconciliation from bottles brought today:
- New: clopidogrel 75 daily, metoprolol succinate 25 daily.
- Changed: atorvastatin now 80 (old 40 bottle set aside, he will not take both).
- Same: aspirin 81, furosemide 40, empagliflozin 10, amlodipine 5, metformin 1000 twice daily, glyburide 5, tamsulosin, finasteride, albuterol as needed.

O: BP and HR as charted, comfortable. Right radial site healing, pulse good. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema.

A/P
1. Inferior STEMI s/p RCA stent: dual antiplatelet therapy, do not miss doses. Statin high intensity now. Beta blocker started. Cardiac rehab referral was sent by the hospital; Marc will call them.
2. HFpEF: compensated.
3. T2DM: glyburide plus a big new list; reviewed hypoglycemia signs again with wife.
4. BMP today.
Records requested again. Cardiology in about 6 weeks. Back here in 1 month.

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
One month out. Hospital records came 8/21 and are reviewed: troponin 8.0, ST elevation inferior leads, RCA stent, echo EF 50% with inferior hypokinesis, discharge list matches what we reconciled.
No chest pain. Energy coming back. Walking 15 minutes twice a day. Rehab intake next week.
BP and HR as charted, no lightheadedness on metoprolol. Lungs clear.
Plan: same list. Cardiology 9/18. Wellness visit with fasting lipids in November.

documents.body: Dilated diabetic exam 09/09/2024. No diabetic retinopathy. Pseudophakia OD, mild nuclear sclerosis OS stable. Recall 1 year.

documents.title: Cardiology follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
Outside cardiology group. Date of visit 09/18/2024.
Seven weeks after inferior STEMI with RCA drug-eluting stent. No angina. Mild fatigue improving. Started cardiac rehab last week, 3 sessions so far.
Meds: aspirin 81, clopidogrel 75, atorvastatin 80, metoprolol succinate 25, furosemide 40, empagliflozin 10, amlodipine 5, metformin, glyburide.
Allergies: ACE inhibitors (cough).
Exam: BP 124/72, HR 64. No JVD. Lungs clear. No edema beyond trace.
Plan: continue dual antiplatelet therapy through 12 months, then aspirin alone. Complete cardiac rehab. Lipids at the PCP's next draw. Return 6 months.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: High-dose flu L arm and updated Moderna R arm. On clopidogrel and aspirin: held pressure 2 min each site, no bruising. Fine at 15 min.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Wife present.
Finished 6 weeks of cardiac rehab, proud of it. No chest pain. No falls.
Function: self-care independent; wife manages meds and appointments.
PHQ-2 1, a little flat after the hospital stay, improving, no plan to treat.
Problem list updated: the August STEMI is now coronary artery disease with an old inferior MI and an RCA stent.
Vaccines: flu and COVID done in October.
Colonoscopy: last 2015 normal; at 73 with heart disease and on two antiplatelets, we agreed no further screening. Wife agrees.
Fasting labs today, first lipids on atorvastatin 80. RTC 3 months.
